scenes.speaker: Narrator
scenes.dialogue: After the violence of 15 July, the movement shifted again. The partial concession of 10 July had not been honored; the police response of 15 July had not contained the anger on the campuses. What had begun as a peaceful student campaign was now entering its most dangerous phase.

scenes.speaker: Narrator
scenes.dialogue: Around noon on 16 July 2024, hundreds of students gathered at Park Mor, the open area adjacent to Gate 1 of Begum Rokeya University in Rangpur, as part of the Anti-Discrimination Student Movement. Law enforcers present at the scene first fired tear gas and sound grenades; most students retreated. Among them was Abu Sayed, an English department student and the movement's local coordinator at the university. Accounts of what happened next differ on the weapon used: Amnesty International's analysis found that police fired shotguns loaded with birdshot at close range; other contemporaneous reporting describes rubber bullets; the findings of a later tribunal describe “multiple gunshot injuries.” The accounts are recorded separately rather than collapsed into a single version.

choice.prompt: Whose account would you like to follow first?

evidence.title: The Scene at Park Mor
evidence.sourceCaption: As reported by The Daily Star retrospective coverage of the July 2024 movement.
evidence.text: Around noon on 16 July 2024, hundreds of students gathered at Park Mor, the open area adjacent to Gate 1 of Begum Rokeya University, Rangpur, as part of the Anti-Discrimination Student Movement. Law enforcers first fired tear gas and sound grenades; most students retreated.

evidence.title: “Buk petechi, guli kor”
evidence.sourceCaption: As reported by The Daily Star retrospective coverage of the July 2024 movement.
evidence.text: Abu Sayed, an English department student and the movement's local coordinator at Begum Rokeya University, did not retreat with the others. Witnesses at the scene describe him standing his ground with arms outstretched, facing the advancing police. The phrase associated with this stance — “Buk petechi, guli kor,” “I have bared my chest — shoot me” — is documented in contemporary reporting and is not invented framing.

evidence.title: Declared Dead at Rangpur Medical College Hospital
evidence.sourceCaption: As reported by The Daily Star retrospective coverage of the July 2024 movement.
evidence.text: Abu Sayed was taken to Rangpur Medical College Hospital, where he was declared dead. He was buried the next day, 17 July 2024, in his ancestral village of Babanpur, Pirganj.

evidence.title: Amnesty International's Findings
evidence.sourceCaption: Amnesty International, investigation into the use of lethal force during the July 2024 Bangladesh protests.
evidence.text: Amnesty International's analysis found that police fired shotguns loaded with birdshot at close range. Other contemporaneous reporting describes rubber bullets. The two accounts describe the same lethal-force incident at Park Mor but differ on the specific weapon.

evidence.title: The Tribunal's Findings
evidence.sourceCaption: Findings of the tribunal investigating the killing of Abu Sayed, as cited in reporting on the case.
evidence.text: The tribunal's findings describe “multiple gunshot injuries,” and the body of findings found no lawful or proportionate justification for the use of lethal force, rejecting claims that the killing occurred during an armed confrontation.

evidence.title: A Widely Circulated Video, and What It Became
evidence.sourceCaption: Cross-referenced from the Wikipedia article 'Killing of Abu Sayed,' used here as a secondary check rather than a primary source.
evidence.text: The events at Park Mor were captured on a widely circulated video. The recording, and the stance Abu Sayed is described as taking in it, became a defining symbol of the July 2024 uprising.
